description: ICS Village brings together operators, researchers, and government leaders to address critical infrastructure defense, industrial control systems security, turbine controls, OT forensics, and active defense.

talks.title: 5 Quick Wins for Improving ICS Cybersecurity Posture
talks.teaser: Outlines five practical and high-impact security wins for strengthening industrial control system defenses.

talks.title: PowerLine Truck Hacking: 2TOOLS4PLC4TRUCKS
talks.teaser: Introduces two open tools for auditing and testing power-line communications and PLCs in heavy-duty vehicles.

talks.title: Keynote
talks.teaser: CISA Director Chris Krebs delivers the opening keynote on defending critical infrastructure and industrial control systems.

talks.title: On the Insecure Nature of Turbine Control Systems
talks.teaser: Examines systemic architectural flaws and insecure-by-design vulnerabilities in turbine control systems.

talks.title: Journey of ICS Project Files: Visibility and Forensics
talks.teaser: Explores parsing proprietary ICS engineering project files to gain deep forensic visibility into industrial controllers.

talks.title: Vulnerability Discovery: Tips for Surviving
talks.teaser: Shares practical survival tips and methodologies for researching and disclosing vulnerabilities in industrial systems.

talks.title: Keynote Q&A
talks.teaser: Chris Krebs answers questions regarding national cyber defense, government coordination, and ICS security.

talks.title: Industrial Cybersecurity in Mexico
talks.teaser: Provides an overview of the industrial cybersecurity landscape, threats, and regulatory status in Mexico.

talks.title: Confessions of an Offensive ICS Researcher
talks.teaser: Reflects on years of offensive ICS research, physical process manipulation attacks, and defensive lessons learned.
talks.summary:
In this introspective presentation from the DEF CON Safe Mode ICS Village, a seasoned industrial penetration tester presents "Confessions of an Offensive ICS Researcher," detailing the transition from offensive vulnerability discovery to managing an enterprise cybersecurity program. Opening at 00:19, the speaker reflects on how offensive security mindsets often diverge from operational realities.

At 05:01, the presenter explains that while offensive researchers naturally focus on high-severity zero-day exploits, industrial defenders face complex operational constraints including regulatory compliance, patch validation, and 24/7 continuous uptime requirements.

Past 20:00 and 40:00, the talk explores real-world case studies of finding vulnerabilities in programmable logic controllers (PLCs) and supervisory systems. The speaker details the friction of coordinating disclosures with industrial hardware vendors and offers practical advice on translating red team findings into actionable, risk-prioritized engineering remediations. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: MITRE ICS ATT&CK
talks.teaser: Introduces the MITRE ATT&CK for Industrial Control Systems knowledge base and its application to threat modeling.

talks.title: ICS SecOps Active Defense Concept with Effective Incident Response
talks.teaser: Presents an active defense concept tailored for ICS security operations to enable rapid and effective incident response.

talks.title: Playing with Electricity
talks.teaser: Explores security research and vulnerabilities in electrical power distribution systems and substations.

talks.title: Operationalizing Cyber Norms
talks.teaser: Discusses operationalizing international cyber norms and rules of engagement to protect civilian critical infrastructure.
talks.summary:
In this international policy and security briefing from the DEF CON Safe Mode ICS Village, a reformed hacker and critical infrastructure specialist presents "Operationalizing Cyber Norms" live from Amsterdam. Opening at 00:00, the speaker explores how geopolitical tensions and state-sponsored cyber operations threaten civilian critical infrastructure.

At 02:01 and 03:00, the talk examines landmark international governance efforts, focusing on the 2015 United Nations Group of Governmental Experts (UN GGE) consensus report that established voluntary non-binding norms prohibiting cyberattacks against critical infrastructure.

At 04:00, the presenter references major historical incidents—including the 2012 Shamoon attacks against Saudi Aramco and attacks on power grids—to underscore the stakes. Concluding past 15:00, the speaker details how to operationalize diplomatic norms through regional CERT cooperation, mandatory incident transparency, and cross-border technical defense pacts. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Vivisecting PowerPC
talks.teaser: Demonstrates binary analysis and reverse engineering techniques targeting PowerPC firmware commonly found in industrial gear.

talks.title: Building a Physical Testbed for Blackstart Restoration
talks.teaser: Details the design and implementation of a physical electric grid testbed for researching blackstart restoration procedures.

talks.title: Mission Kill: Process Targeting in ICS Attacks
talks.teaser: Analyzes how sophisticated adversaries design malware to target industrial physical processes and induce mission kills.
